Actual cutoffs are determined each cycle by the number of available places (a quota) against the number and strength of that cycle's applicant pool, and can move up or down year to year and round to round; universities and TACs themselves describe published thresholds as a guide, not a promise. This makes the Australian model, for the large majority of programmes, a genuinely capacity-constrained ranked-allocation system — closer in structural spirit to a rolling, demand-responsive clearing process than either the Netherlands' 'eligible functionally equals admitted' non-numerus-fixus model or a fully holistic US-style review. Meeting a subject-prerequisite/assumed-knowledge bar and holding a recognized qualification establishes eligibility; whether that translates into an actual offer depends on where the applicant's selection rank falls relative to that specific cycle's other applicants for that specific course, knowable only after the fact. Restricted programmes (Medicine) layer a genuine capacity ceiling and multi-criteria selection (test plus interview) on top of this already-competitive baseline.

safe_inferences: It is safe to infer that no single national admissions platform or decision-making body exists anywhere in the Australian system — five separate state-based TACs plus direct-to-university application both coexist, and which applies depends on the applicant's qualification type and the target university's state.
It is safe to infer that a TAC's role, wherever one is involved, is registration/rank-calculation/administration, never the admission decision itself, which always sits with the university.

It is safe to infer that the ATAR is a cohort-relative rank built only from completed final results, never a prediction, and is therefore not comparable across different states/cohorts/years without a specific published conversion mechanism, and is never a GPA.

It is safe to infer that a plain Turkish MEB Lise Diploması, considered alone, will not receive a centrally calculated selection rank from UAC specifically (explicitly listed as not-assessed), and that a Turkish applicant should independently verify each target university's own direct-assessment policy rather than assuming a uniform Australia-wide position.
It is safe to infer that a published ATAR/selection-rank cutoff for a course is a retrospective data point, not a forward guarantee, for the large majority of Australian programmes.

It is safe to infer that recommendation letters are not a standard requirement, and that extracurricular activity and personal statements are not part of the core ATAR/selection-rank mechanism, mattering only within specific named schemes at specific universities.
unsafe_inferences: Do not assume Australia has one national admissions system or timeline merely because a national-sounding rank (ATAR) exists — it is calculated and administered separately by five different state bodies with materially different rules on which applicants and qualifications they even process.

Do not assume UAC's specific overseas-qualification policies (its accepted list, its IB/Combined-Rank mechanism, its 'will not assess' Turkish-diploma position) generalize to VTAC, QTAC, SATAC, or TISC — VTAC was directly confirmed to process no overseas qualification centrally at all, a materially different position from UAC's.

Do not assume the Turkish High School Diploma is rejected by every Australian university — UAC's finding is that its own member institutions won't process it centrally through UAC; individual universities' own direct-application discretion was not shown to be a blanket rejection.
Do not assume a published ATAR cutoff/selection rank for a course this year will hold next year, or even in the next offer round of the same year — it is demand-responsive, not fixed.
Do not assume SAT/ACT-style testing matters broadly — it appears only as one narrow equivalency-evidence item on an overseas-qualifications list.

Do not assume UCAT ANZ and ISAT are interchangeable or that either applies to every Medicine programme uniformly — several universities require different tests for domestic/NZ vs. international applicants specifically, and undergraduate-entry Medicine (UCAT ANZ/ISAT) is a structurally different pathway from graduate-entry Medicine (GAMSAT).
Do not assume the 'Genuine Student' visa personal-statement requirement is part of the academic admissions decision — it is a separate, government-run immigration assessment.

eligibility_competitiveness_fit.eligibility: Holding a recognized qualification (Australian Year 12, a TAC/university-accepted overseas equivalent, or IB/A-Level etc.) and meeting the specific programme's subject prerequisites (not merely its softer assumed-knowledge guidance) — a checkable, largely binary gate, evaluated per-TAC-or-university depending on qualification type and target state.
eligibility_competitiveness_fit.competitiveness: Unlike the Netherlands' non-numerus-fixus model, competitiveness is not confined to a narrow set of restricted programmes in Australia — it is the default mechanism for the large majority of courses via the floating selection-rank-cutoff system, making 'eligible' and 'admitted' genuinely different, non-equivalent states for essentially every programme, not just Medicine-style restricted ones. This is a meaningfully different eligibility-competitiveness relationship from the Netherlands (where the two collapse into one for most programmes) and should be represented as such in ORYN's model — closer in structure to the UK/US pattern of this research package than to the Dutch one, despite Australia's qualification-threshold-style surface mechanics.
eligibility_competitiveness_fit.fit: Expressed mainly through the prerequisite/assumed-knowledge subject match at the general level; genuine holistic/narrative fit assessment (personal statements, interviews, portfolios) is concentrated in specific schemes and programme types (EAS, EAPL, early-offer schemes, Medicine, creative/performance programmes) rather than functioning as a universal layer.

counselor_actions: Identify which state/territory (and therefore which TAC — UAC/VTAC/QTAC/SATAC/TISC, or none) each target university sits in before assuming a single national process; this determines whether an overseas qualification (IB especially) is processed centrally with a Combined-Rank conversion or must go direct to the university.

For a Turkish MEB-only student with no supplementary qualification: flag early that UAC will not centrally assess a plain Lise Diploması, verify whether the specific target university (regardless of state) has its own case-by-case pathway or published threshold, and treat a supplementary IB/A-Level/AP qualification or a foundation-year programme (e.g. Melbourne's Trinity College Foundation Studies) as the most reliably documented routes — planned well in advance.

For IB students: confirm whether the target university's state TAC processes IB centrally (and via which conversion) or requires direct application, and check whether the applicant's exam session (May vs November) and Semester 1 vs Semester 2 target intake create a predicted-grades need.
Never present a published ATAR/selection-rank cutoff as a guaranteed threshold — treat it as last cycle's outcome and build in a buffer, especially for oversubscribed courses.

For Medicine/Dentistry-track students: plan the UCAT ANZ (or confirm ISAT if applying as an international student) sitting many months ahead of the general application cycle, confirm which specific test the target university requires for the applicant's own status (domestic/NZ vs international), and clarify early whether the student is pursuing undergraduate-entry (UCAT ANZ/ISAT) or graduate-entry (GAMSAT, after a bachelor's) Medicine, since these are different multi-year plans.
Confirm each target programme's actual subject prerequisite (not just its softer assumed-knowledge guidance) and verify the student's coursework satisfies it.

If pursuing a bonus-points/adjustment-factor scheme (subject-based, equity/EAS, or elite-achievement-based like UNSW's EAPL), confirm which body administers it (TAC vs. university) and whether the specific target institution actually accepts it — some institutions opt out of EAS entirely.
Keep the student-visa Genuine Student requirement conceptually and procedurally separate from the academic admissions process when advising international families.

data_model_implications.notes: Australia requires a state/TAC-aware layer between country and university, structurally similar to Canada's province-aware layer but with a sharper practical consequence: in Australia, the same qualification (most clearly, an overseas-completed IB Diploma) is processed through a centralized rank-conversion mechanism at UAC-affiliated institutions and through a fully direct, TAC-free pathway at VTAC-affiliated institutions — this needs to be modeled as a first-class (qualification type x target-state-TAC) -> processing-pathway variation, not folded into a single 'how Australia treats the IB' fact. The ATAR/selection rank itself needs to be modeled as a non-portable, time-bound, retrospective value — meaningful only within a specific state/cohort/year, never a fixed eligibility threshold and never directly comparable to another state's ATAR without an explicit conversion step. The Turkish MEB Lise Diploması needs a platform-scoped negative flag ('not centrally assessed by UAC') kept distinct from a country-wide negative flag ('rejected by all Australian universities') — the evidence supports only the former. Restricted-programme modeling needs to distinguish government-funding-driven capacity caps (Medicine's CSP allocation) from the general demand-driven floating-cutoff mechanism that applies to essentially every other course — these are different mechanisms with different modeling implications (a hard ceiling vs. a re-computed-each-cycle market-clearing rank), even though both ultimately produce 'not every eligible applicant gets in.'
gaps: No official primary source was found confirming or denying whether QTAC, SATAC, or TISC extend a UAC-style centralized overseas-qualification/IB processing mechanism, or instead mirror VTAC's fully-direct approach — only UAC and VTAC's contrasting positions were directly confirmed.

No individual Go8 university's own numeric Turkey-specific equivalency threshold (paralleling the Netherlands' Tilburg/VU examples) was located in this pass; University of Melbourne's dedicated recognised-qualifications page blocked automated fetch.
The precise current mechanics of VTAC's own referenced 'interstate and NZ' ATAR-comparability process were not independently verified in depth.

Whether a current-day Australian body plays a Nuffic/Anabin/CIMEA-equivalent role specifically for higher-education admission recognition (distinct from the AQF's qualification-levels framework or migration-focused skills-assessment infrastructure) was not conclusively determined — UAC's own methodology leaning on the UK's NARIC/UCAS suggests the answer may be 'no dedicated Australian equivalent,' but this was not exhaustively ruled out.

system_university_programme_override_mod.explanation: Layer 1 (national): genuinely thin. No national admissions platform or decision-making body exists; the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) standardizes Australia's own qualification levels but is not a foreign-credential evaluator or an admissions mechanism; Commonwealth Supported Place funding policy is a national government lever that shapes capacity indirectly (and, for Medicine specifically, directly and explicitly), without itself making any admission decision. Layer 2 (state/TAC): UAC, VTAC, QTAC, SATAC, TISC — each independently scoped to its own state/territory, each calculating or receiving the ATAR for its own jurisdiction, administering preference lists and multi-round offers, and (for UAC and QTAC specifically, evidenced in this research) running Educational Access Scheme/equity-adjustment administration on behalf of member universities — but these TACs materially differ from each other in scope, most sharply in which qualification types they will process at all (UAC's ~40-qualification accepted list plus its IB/Combined-Rank mechanism vs. VTAC's Australian/NZ-only processing). Layer 3 (university): the actual admission decision always sits here — floating selection-rank cutoffs, direct international-application processing and qualification assessment (especially outside UAC's remit), English-language thresholds, predicted-grades acceptance policy, and adoption/design of bonus-point schemes (UNSW's HSC Plus and EAPL, each with their own point caps and exclusion lists) are all set independently per institution, and an institution can opt out of a TAC-administered scheme entirely (several universities do not accept QTAC's EAS). Layer 4 (programme): subject prerequisites vs. assumed knowledge, Medicine/Dentistry's test-plus-interview requirement (and which specific test applies to which applicant type), portfolio/audition requirements, and undergraduate-direct-entry vs. graduate-entry-only structuring are all set at this level. ORYN should never present a Layer 3 or Layer 4 fact as if it were a Layer 1 or Layer 2 national or state-wide fact — and, specific to Australia, should never assume a Layer 2 (TAC) fact from one state transfers to another state's TAC.

matrix_row.main_application_architecture: No single national platform or admissions body; five state/territory-based Tertiary Admissions Centres (UAC, VTAC, QTAC, SATAC, TISC) handle registration and ATAR calculation for domestic (and some international) applicants, while admission decisions remain fully with each university; most overseas-qualification holders apply directly to each university instead of through a TAC
matrix_row.central_platform: None national. State-based: UAC (NSW/ACT), VTAC (Victoria), QTAC (Queensland), SATAC (SA/NT), TISC (WA) — genuinely separate platforms with different rules, not one federated system
matrix_row.direct_applications_possible: Yes, and the norm for most overseas-qualification holders — VTAC explicitly restricts its own processing to Australian/NZ-completed Year 12, VCE and IB only; UAC is the exception in also centrally processing a defined list of ~40 overseas qualifications (excluding the Turkish diploma) plus IB wherever completed
matrix_row.application_choice_limits: UAC: 5 preferences (domestic), 6 (international/postgraduate); QTAC: 6 preferences; no preference cap for direct university applications, though ANU caps 3 programmes per paid application (soft, fee-driven, not rule-driven)
matrix_row.predicted_grades_role: No native ATAR concept — ATAR is calculated only from actual final Year 12 results, never a prediction; foreign predicted grades (chiefly IB) are read operationally by universities (e.g. University of Melbourne) to support conditional offers before final results are released
matrix_row.subject_prerequisites: Real and programme-specific, expressed as a hard 'prerequisite' (must-complete-to-a-stated-standard) distinct from softer 'assumed knowledge' (recommended, not required) — the same input subject can be a prerequisite at one university/programme and merely assumed knowledge at another
matrix_row.standardized_tests: Not required generally; SAT appears only as one accepted US-diploma-adjacent equivalency item on UAC's list; UCAT ANZ (domestic/NZ) or ISAT (international) plus interview required for Medicine/Dentistry/some clinical-science programmes at a defined consortium of universities
matrix_row.language_proof: IELTS/TOEFL iBT/PTE/Cambridge/Duolingo, university- and programme-set (Go8 commonly ~IELTS 6.5-7.0); a separate, generally lower, student-visa English threshold (subclass 500) applies at the immigration stage, distinct from the academic admission requirement
matrix_row.essays_motivation: Not required for standard ATAR/selection-rank or direct-qualification-based entry; appears only in specific schemes (Educational Access Scheme disadvantage statements, UNSW's Elite Athletes/Performers/Leaders scheme) and separately in the student-visa Genuine Student assessment, which is an immigration fact, not an admissions one
matrix_row.recommendations: Not identified as a standard requirement in any source reviewed — consistent with a transcript/qualification-driven rather than reference-driven system
matrix_row.extracurricular_role: Not a factor in the core ATAR/selection-rank mechanism; can matter at specific university-run schemes (e.g. UNSW's Elite Athletes, Performers and Leaders bonus-points scheme) or some early-offer/non-ATAR pathways — genuinely institution-dependent, not a national feature
matrix_row.conditional_offers: Yes, chiefly for applicants whose final results are not yet available (predicted-grade IB applicants; early-offer/Year-11-based schemes; foundation-pathway progression) — not the universal defining mechanic it is in the UK
matrix_row.restricted_programmes: Medicine (and Dentistry) is the clearest capacity-capped field: government sets a fixed Commonwealth Supported Place allocation specifically for medicine (unlike the dollars-based, place-uncapped funding of most other fields), clinical-placement capacity is genuinely limited, and UCAT ANZ/ISAT plus interview gate entry on top of ATAR/selection rank
matrix_row.turkiye_meb_direct_entry_complexity: High: UAC (NSW/ACT) explicitly places the Turkish High School Diploma in its 'will not be assessed' category, meaning no centralized selection-rank conversion is available for a plain MEB Lise Diploması; no Go8 university-specific numeric equivalency table was found in this pass, so affected applicants likely need a supplementary qualification (IB/A-Level/AP, all separately well-accepted) or a foundation-year pathway, verified per target university
matrix_row.dominant_counselor_risk: Assuming a published 'selection rank'/ATAR cutoff is a fixed eligibility threshold rather than last year's floating, supply-and-demand-driven outcome — and, specific to overseas qualifications, assuming one state's Tertiary Admissions Centre policy (e.g. UAC's centralized overseas-qualification processing) generalizes to another state's (VTAC processes no overseas qualification at all, IB included, unless completed in Australia/NZ)

unresolved_questions: Whether any individual Group of Eight (or other) Australian university publishes its own specific numeric equivalency threshold for the Turkish Lise Diploması, in the style of the Netherlands' Tilburg/VU examples — not confirmed in this pass (University of Melbourne's dedicated recognised-qualifications page blocked automated fetch; no ANU or Sydney Turkey-specific published page was located).

Whether QTAC, SATAC, and TISC mirror UAC's centralized overseas-qualification processing (including its IB mechanism and its explicit Turkish-diploma exclusion) or instead mirror VTAC's fully-direct-to-university approach for non-Australian/NZ qualifications — only UAC and VTAC's contrasting positions were directly confirmed via primary sources this pass.
Whether the 2024-reported government proposal for a hard cap on total domestic-plus-international student places has since been legislated or implemented as of the current (2026-27) cycle.

The exact, currently-published domestic-vs-international UCAT-ANZ/ISAT split at each individual UCAT ANZ consortium university — confirmed for a named handful (Monash, UNSW, UTAS, UWA, Western Sydney) but not exhaustively verified across the full consortium.

Whether YKS plays any role, however indirect, in any Australian university's individual (non-UAC-list) recognition decision for a Turkish applicant — absence of evidence in sources reviewed, not a confirmed-irrelevant finding.
The precise current mechanics of VTAC's referenced 'interstate and NZ' ATAR-comparability process.

Whether a current-day Australian body exists that plays a Nuffic/Anabin/CIMEA-equivalent role specifically for higher-education admission recognition (as opposed to the AQF's qualification-levels framework or migration-focused skills-assessment infrastructure) — UAC's own methodology leaning on the UK's NARIC/UCAS suggests the answer may genuinely be 'no dedicated Australian equivalent,' but this was not exhaustively ruled out.
Precise, currently-published Go8-wide English-language (IELTS/TOEFL/PTE) thresholds beyond the aggregated secondary-corroborated range cited above.

A_admissions_architecture.primary_application_route: There is no single national application platform for France; which platform applies is determined by the applicant's diploma track and, for foreign-diploma holders, their country of residence. Parcoursup is the mandatory registration-and-routing platform for anyone preparing or holding a French or European Baccalauréat -- French nationals, foreign nationals enrolled in a French lycée (in France or abroad, e.g. an AEFE-network school), and EU/EEA/Swiss/Monaco/Andorra citizens generally, regardless of nationality. Like Studielink in the Netherlands, Parcoursup itself makes no admission decisions for 'formations sélectives' (CPGE, BTS, BUT, most Grande École/business/engineering-school 'vœux', IFSI, PASS/LAS) -- each formation ranks candidates using its own confidential 'algorithme local' or a selection commission; Parcoursup is the submission/routing/response layer, not the decision-maker. For ordinary ('non sélective') Licences, admission is closer to a right once eligibility is met, but the 2018 'loi ORE' (Orientation et Réussite des Étudiants) lets a université rank candidates against the Licence mention's published 'attendus' whenever demand exceeds capacity ('licence en tension'), even though the Licence is not formally classified sélective. Foreign-diploma holders (no French/European Bac) generally do not use Parcoursup for ordinary Licence entry at all -- they file a DAP (Demande d'Admission Préalable) dossier instead, either electronically via their country's Campus France portal (if resident in one of 72 'Études en France' countries -- Türkiye confirmed on this list) or on paper directly with the French embassy/consulate's cultural cooperation service (if resident elsewhere).
A_admissions_architecture.centralized_or_decentralized: Hybrid and track-dependent in a way more complex than any other country in this package. For the French/European-Bac track: registration is centralized (Parcoursup), but admission decisions for sélective formations are fully decentralized to each formation's own selection process, while ordinary Licences apply a right-based threshold that can quietly become decentralized ranking under the loi ORE when a Licence is 'en tension'. For the foreign-diploma track: DAP dossiers are routed through a second, entirely different centralized-routing layer (the Études en France/Campus France platform, for residents of listed countries) or handled fully locally (embassy-filed paper DAP elsewhere), with the substantive decision made independently by each of up to 3 chosen universities' own admissions commission.
major_application_platforms: Parcoursup (parcoursup.gouv.fr) -- mandatory for French/European Baccalauréat track applicants; registration/routing only, not itself a decision-maker

Études en France / Campus France (pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr, plus country-specific portals such as turquie.campusfrance.org) -- for foreign-diploma applicants resident in one of 72 listed countries, carries the DAP dossier and, separately, visa-linked administrative processing
Paper DAP filed directly with the French embassy/consulate's service de coopération et d'action culturelle -- for foreign-diploma applicants resident outside the 72 listed countries

Direct institutional portals (e.g. admission.sciencespo.fr for Sciences Po's Bachelor 'voie internationale'; École Polytechnique's own Bachelor of Science admissions process) -- a small number of elite institutions run fully separate applications for foreign-diploma applicants, bypassing both Parcoursup and DAP for the admissions decision itself
A_admissions_architecture.direct_university_application_possible: Not as a general alternative for French/European Bac holders (Parcoursup is required) or for most foreign-diploma holders resident in an Études-en-France-listed country (the DAP/Campus France process is required). A small number of elite institutions -- confirmed for Sciences Po's Bachelor international track and, by pattern, École Polytechnique's Bachelor of Science -- run their own direct application portal specifically for foreign-diploma applicants, entirely outside both Parcoursup and DAP for the substantive admissions decision. Sciences Po itself splits by diploma type, not nationality or residence: any applicant preparing a French or European Baccalauréat (including a non-French national at a French lycée abroad) must use Parcoursup for Sciences Po, while any applicant preparing a genuinely foreign secondary diploma applies through Sciences Po's own separate international portal -- confirmed directly from Sciences Po's own admissions pages.
A_admissions_architecture.application_limit_if_any: Two structurally different caps depending on track. Parcoursup: maximum 10 vœux, with up to 20 sous-vœux across grouped establishments within those vœux, and no required ranking/ordering of preferences. DAP: maximum 3 university choices, set in law (Article D.612-16, Code de l'éducation) -- read directly from the official 2026-2027 DAP CERFA form -- a materially lower ceiling than Parcoursup's 10 for the same admissions cycle. No cap was found on Sciences Po's or École Polytechnique's separate direct-application portals (single-institution applications, not multi-choice platforms).
A_admissions_architecture.parallel_application_rules: A given applicant is very unlikely to need more than one track simultaneously, since the applicable track is generally determined by diploma type (and, for foreign-diploma holders, residence) rather than free choice. No evidence was found of an overall cap spanning Parcoursup, DAP, and a direct-institution application together for the same applicant in one cycle. Foreign-diploma applicants resident in an Études-en-France country who are admitted through a direct-institution portal (e.g. Sciences Po) likely still need to complete Études en France separately afterward for visa processing specifically -- this exact interaction was not confirmed by a single source covering both steps together this session.
A_admissions_architecture.scope: national (loi ORE, Article D.612-16, the Études-en-France country list) / platform (Parcoursup vs. Études en France/DAP are two structurally different platforms) / university (Sciences Po's and Polytechnique's separate direct portals)

B_qualification_eligibility.recognition_mechanism: For French/European Bac holders there is no separate 'equivalence' step: the Baccalauréat (or a recognized European equivalent) simultaneously functions as secondary-school-leaving diploma and higher-education access credential, and Parcoursup is the access mechanism directly. For foreign-diploma holders, France has no single national comparability baseline equivalent to the Netherlands' Nuffic or Germany's Anabin that every university consults before deciding. Instead, the official DAP form's own 'Situation A/B/C' framework governs the dossier: does the applicant's diploma give direct access to higher education in their own country? Situation A (yes) requires only transcripts and the diploma; Situation B (no) additionally requires an 'attestation d'accès à l'enseignement supérieur' from the home country's own authorities (evidence of passing a competitive exam, special test, or interview); Situation B3 covers applicants who have already obtained that home-country access attestation. The admitting université's own admissions commission then evaluates the full dossier against its published 'capacités d'accueil' -- a case-by-case, university-level judgment, not a centralized ruling.
B_qualification_eligibility.baseline_qualification_expectation: Baccalauréat Général (or Technologique/Professionnel, out of scope here) for the French/European-Bac/Parcoursup track. For the DAP/foreign-diploma track, the baseline is simply 'a secondary school-leaving diploma,' with the DAP Situation A/B/C framework determining what supplementary evidence is required rather than a single pass/fail equivalence threshold.
B_qualification_eligibility.subject_prerequisites_general: See dedicated subject_prerequisites section: nationally-published 'attendus' per Licence mention, explicitly framed as non-exclusionary guidance rather than a hard gate, with individual sélective formations able to bind their own local requirements more tightly.
B_qualification_eligibility.equivalency_process: For foreign-diploma/DAP-track applicants, no pre-approved 'diploma finder' list equivalent to Dutch universities' country-specific diploma pages was identified this session. The DAP dossier itself, evaluated directly by the target université's admissions commission, appears to be the operative mechanism rather than a prior centralized comparability step.
B_qualification_eligibility.university_discretion: Substantial for DAP-track applicants: each of up to 3 chosen universities evaluates the same dossier independently against its own stated capacity, though this research did not surface a Tilburg-vs-VU-style paired example of differing thresholds for the same foreign diploma at two named French universities this session -- a gap relative to the Netherlands entry's depth on this specific point.

credentials_covered.turkiye_meb: Turkish 'Lise Diploması' -- see dedicated turkiye_applicant_view section. Not confirmed as DAP Situation A or B by a Turkey-naming source; reasoned toward Situation B by analogy to R2.1's YKS findings.
credentials_covered.ib_diploma: Not independently re-verified for France this session; IB Diploma holders preparing outside the French system would generally be foreign-diploma/DAP-track (or, at Sciences Po specifically, explicitly named as eligible for the international track) rather than Parcoursup-track, unless the IB is taken alongside or in place of the Bac at a French-system school.
credentials_covered.a_levels: Not independently re-verified for France this session; A-Level holders are explicitly named as an eligible diploma type on Sciences Po's international-track admissions page.
credentials_covered.us_diploma: Explicitly named as an eligible diploma type (with AP scores) on Sciences Po's international-track admissions page; general DAP-track treatment for other universities not independently re-verified this session.
credentials_covered.german_abitur: Explicitly named as an eligible diploma type on Sciences Po's international-track admissions page; general DAP-track treatment for other universities not independently re-verified this session.

turkiye_applicant_view.standard_diploma_sufficient_for_direct_e: Not directly comparable to a 'sufficient/insufficient' single answer the way the Netherlands' VWO-equivalence question is, because a plain MEB Lise Diploması holder resident in Türkiye is generally not on the Parcoursup/Bac-equivalence track at all -- Türkiye is primary-source-confirmed (the official 2026-2027 DAP 'Dossier Blanc' CERFA form, n° 50845#25) as one of 72 'Espaces Campus France à procédure Études en France' countries. The applicable pathway is the DAP dossier, filed electronically via turquie.campusfrance.org, capped at 3 university choices, with each chosen université's own admissions commission deciding independently against its stated capacity -- the platform itself changes for a Turkish applicant relative to a French-Bac holder, not just an equivalence threshold within one platform.
turkiye_applicant_view.additional_qualifications_commonly_requi: A Turkish DAP applicant must generally pass the TCF (Test de Connaissance du Français), 'tout public' version with a mandatory written-expression component, unless independently exempted (DELF/DALF B2+, or substantially French-medium prior schooling) -- Türkiye is not on the DAP form's list of exclusively-French-official-language countries. Whether the MEB Lise Diploması alone falls under DAP 'Situation A' (direct access to Turkish higher education) or 'Situation B' (does not, requiring a supplementary home-country access attestation) was not confirmed by a source naming Turkey specifically.
turkiye_applicant_view.ap_ib_a_level_impact: Not confirmed either way for France this session. R2.1's Turkish MEB research and this session's French research were not able to establish whether an AP/IB/A-Level qualification layered on top of a Turkish MEB record materially eases DAP admission the way it clearly does at Dutch universities (see netherlands.md) -- flagged as a genuine unresolved question, not assumed to transfer.
turkiye_applicant_view.national_entrance_exam_relevance: Reasoned inference, not primary-confirmed: combining the DAP form's own Situation A/B framework with R2.1's established finding that Turkish higher-education placement requires the separate national YKS exam (a MEB Lise Diploması alone does not itself grant a Turkish university place), a Turkish DAP applicant plausibly falls under Situation B and would likely need to supply YKS-based evidence of access to Turkish higher education. No source naming Turkey specifically in the DAP context was found to confirm this.
turkiye_applicant_view.foundation_year_common: No France-specific foundation-year bridge mechanism (comparable to the Netherlands' 'one year of Turkish Lisans credits' route) was identified this session -- a genuine gap, not a confirmed absence.
turkiye_applicant_view.recognition_centralized_or_university_sp: University-specific in the sense that each of up to 3 chosen universities' own admissions commission evaluates the DAP dossier independently against its own stated capacity, but there is also a genuinely distinct national/platform layer not present in the Netherlands case: which platform applies at all (DAP/Études en France vs. Parcoursup) is itself centrally determined by the applicant's diploma type and residence, before any university-level judgment begins. No ENIC-NARIC France page specifically addressing Turkish Lise Diploması comparability was found or fetchable this session (enic-naric.fr failed with a certificate error) -- a genuine gap, not a confirmed 'not used' finding.

academic_evidence_used.transcript_role: For French-Bac/Parcoursup-track applicants: the livret scolaire (actual première/terminale bulletin grades, 0-20 scale) is submitted and read by admissions commissions before final Bac results exist. For DAP-track applicants: transcripts covering the last two academic years plus the first trimester of the current year are required (Situation A1/B1), or the final diploma's own results record (Situation A2/B2/B3) -- read directly from the official DAP CERFA form.
academic_evidence_used.native_grades_handling: Native grades are read on their original scale by the relevant admissions commission -- French Bac grades on the standard 0-20 scale (per R2.1), foreign DAP-track grades on their own native scale with no universal conversion table identified. No authoritative cross-system GPA conversion exists for either track, consistent with this package's cross-country pattern (RULE-ADMISSIONS-004).
academic_evidence_used.predicted_grades_role: No formal numeric predicted-grade concept exists nationally; see dedicated predicted_grades section for the Fiche Avenir's qualitative near-equivalent function for the Parcoursup track.
academic_evidence_used.final_grades_role: Final Bac results are required for definitive enrolment but are not yet available at the point most Parcoursup admission decisions are made (Bac finals land in June/July; Parcoursup's admission phase begins 2 June). For DAP-track applicants, the original diploma is required only 'au moment de l'inscription définitive' (at final registration), confirmed directly from the official CERFA form -- a genuine diploma-conditional structure.
academic_evidence_used.external_exams_role: For French-Bac students, the Bac's own spécialité written exams (March of terminale) and the épreuves anticipées de français (end of première) are the primary externally-graded signal, per R2.1 -- read by admissions commissions where already available at the time of Parcoursup dossier review. For DAP-track applicants, whatever externally-set exams are part of their own home curriculum are represented through the diploma/transcript record itself, not through a separate French external-exam layer.
academic_evidence_used.course_rigor_signal: For French-Bac-track applicants: which two of three spécialités were retained through terminale is the primary legible rigor/alignment signal (per R2.1), read against the target Licence mention's or CPGE's published attendus. No equivalent nationally-mapped foreign-curriculum rigor signal was identified for DAP-track applicants.
academic_evidence_used.standardized_tests: See dedicated standardized_tests section -- no SAT/ACT-equivalent nationally; TCF is a mandatory language-and-writing gate specifically for most DAP-track applicants.

predicted_grades.are_used: Not as a formal, UK-style numeric predicted grade -- confirmed both by R2.1's prior research and directly by the Ministry of Education's own Fiche Avenir document read in full this session. The functionally closest mechanism for French-Bac-track applicants is the combination of the livret scolaire's actual in-progress première/terminale grades plus the Fiche Avenir's qualitative appraisal -- both read by admissions commissions before final Bac results exist, which is close in function (though not in form) to a predicted-grade mechanism.
predicted_grades.where: The Fiche Avenir, read from the official Ministry PDF: a vœu-specific, entirely dematerialized document combining (1) a common appraisal from the professeur principal covering méthode de travail, autonomie, capacité à s'investir, and engagements et responsabilités; (2) the chef d'établissement's opinion on the candidate's 'capacité à réussir' in the specific formation plus an indication of class level; (3) optional per-discipline teacher comments on post-Bac orientation. As of the 2025 platform change, numeric data (rank, class average, cohort size) travels with the bulletins themselves, not the Fiche Avenir.
predicted_grades.by_whom: The professeur principal (or professeur référent) and the chef d'établissement, per lycée, for every candidate in Terminale (Générale, Technologique, Professionnelle) and equivalent tracks (Brevet des Métiers d'Art, Brevet Professionnel, Brevet de Technicien) plus bridging classes -- confirmed directly from the official Ministry document.
predicted_grades.for_what: To give the admissions commission a qualitative read on likely success before final Bac results are known, since Parcoursup's admission phase (from 2 June) begins before Bac finals (June/July) are complete.
predicted_grades.conditional_offer_relationship: Indirect but real: the Fiche Avenir and livret scolaire inform the sélective-formation ranking decision itself, while the formal conditional mechanism for not-yet-final results is Parcoursup's 'oui, si' response type (see conditional_vs_unconditional_admission) and, for the DAP track, the explicit diploma-conditional Situation A1/B1 structure.
predicted_grades.final_result_requirement: Yes -- for DAP-track applicants the original diploma is required at final registration, confirmed directly from the CERFA form. For Parcoursup-track applicants, no explicit official statement of the consequence of non-obtention of the Bac was found this session; treated as a reasoned analogy to every other researched country's handling of this, not confirmed for France specifically.

conditional_vs_unconditional_admission.concept_exists: Yes, but in a narrower and structurally different sense than the UK or Netherlands.
conditional_vs_unconditional_admission.explanation: Parcoursup's 'oui, si' response is a distinct, named mechanism: admission conditional not on achieving a target final grade, but on the candidate accepting a mandatory remediation/support pathway ('parcours de consolidation') attached to that place -- a genuinely France-specific conditional-offer flavor not documented elsewhere in this research package. Final Bac attainment itself functions more like an implicit assumption than a formally-labeled conditional artifact in the sources reviewed this session -- no explicit official statement of the consequence of a Parcoursup place if the Bac is not obtained was found. The DAP dossier carries an explicit, confirmed diploma-conditional structure: Situations A1/B1 (diploma still 'en préparation', not yet obtained) are built into the form itself, with the original diploma required only at final registration -- functionally equivalent to the Netherlands' diploma-conditional admission for that specific track.

subject_prerequisites.pattern: The Ministry publishes a national reference framework -- 'attendus nationaux' -- per Licence 'mention' (major) and separately for CPGE, describing expected competencies, knowledge, and subject alignment. This framework is explicitly non-exclusionary by design: official guidance states attendus 'n'ont pas vocation à exclure automatiquement les candidats' (are not meant to automatically exclude candidates), a materially softer instrument than the Netherlands' vakkeneisen or UK 'essential' subject requirements, though individual sélective formations can and do layer their own binding local specifics on top ('chaque établissement définit ses propres attentes'). For French-Bac-track students, the operative legible signal feeding attendus-alignment is which two of three spécialités were retained through terminale.
subject_prerequisites.scope: national (the attendus cadrage framework itself, coordinated by the Ministry with higher-education stakeholders) / formation (each formation's local emphasis and, for sélective formations, its own binding requirements)
illustrative_examples: Licence Psychologie's published attendus emphasize written/oral expression and strong performance in at least two humanities/social-science disciplines.
STEM-adjacent Licences and scientific CPGE commonly look for Mathématiques + Physique-Chimie spécialité retention.
Economics/social-science mentions commonly look for SES + Mathématiques or HGGSP spécialité retention.
subject_prerequisites.attendus_detail: Attendus are coordinated at national level via the Ministry's 'cadrage national des attendus' for Licence mentions and CPGE, then locally interpreted (and, for sélective formations, tightened into binding local requirements) by each formation. No equivalent nationally-published mapping from foreign curricula (A-Level subjects, IB Higher Level subjects, MEB coursework) onto French attendus was found this session -- a genuine gap relative to the Netherlands' explicit foreign-equivalent subject tables (e.g. 'Mathematics B-level, Physics, Chemistry').

standardized_tests.mandatory_optional_status: No SAT/ACT-equivalent exists for ordinary Licence entry, nationally or otherwise. The TCF (Test de Connaissance du Français) functions as a mandatory gate specifically for most DAP-track (foreign-diploma) applicants, read in full from the official CERFA form: 76 multiple-choice questions (oral comprehension, language structures, written comprehension) plus a mandatory written-expression component (three exercises), 2h25 total, fee-based, results valid 2 years, administered by France Éducation international through embassy-designated centers. CPGE-to-Grande-École 'concours' (run by inter-school consortia, roughly two years after CPGE entry) and PASS/LAS second-year 'épreuves' (university-run written-then-oral exam groups) are real, high-stakes, competitive assessments, but both are programme/track-specific, not baseline Licence-entry requirements.
standardized_tests.current_cycle_note: TCF-DAP session dates and prices vary by country/embassy; a Turkish applicant must sit the TCF by 13 February 2026 for the 2026-2027 DAP cycle to obtain results before university commissions begin around 16 March 2026, per the official CERFA calendar.
programme_specific_tests: TCF TP (tout public) avec épreuve d'expression écrite obligatoire -- mandatory French-language and writing test for most DAP-track applicants, results scored 0-699 (QCM) plus a level A1-C2 and a separate /20 written-expression score.
CPGE-to-Grande-École concours -- bespoke, consortium/school-specific entrance exams sat after 2 years of CPGE, not sat at CPGE-entry stage itself.

PASS/LAS second-year 'groupes d'épreuves' -- university-run continuous-assessment-plus-written-exam group, then an oral-exam group for the mid-ranking band, determining rank-order admission to MMOPK second year.

language_requirements.framework: For DAP-track applicants: TCF as described in standardized_tests, required unless exempted. Confirmed exemption categories, read directly from the official CERFA form: nationals/residents of countries where French is the exclusive official language and whose diploma is from such a country; candidates whose secondary education was substantially conducted in French; candidates who attended a French-language secondary school on a jointly-published Ministry list; holders of a qualifying French-language diploma at CEFR B2 or above (DELF/DALF); candidates scoring at or above 400/699 on the Paris-Île-de-France CCI's 'Test d'évaluation de français'. French/European-Bac/Parcoursup-track applicants face no general French-proficiency test, since they are already schooled in French.
language_requirements.exemption_pattern: Türkiye is not on the DAP form's list of exclusively- or non-exclusively-French-official-language countries, so a Turkish DAP applicant generally must sit the TCF unless independently DELF/DALF-B2-plus certified or otherwise substantially French-schooled.
language_requirements.where_variation_begins: English-taught-programme language requirements (IELTS/TOEFL/Duolingo, for the minority of French programmes taught in English, including some Sciences Po and Grande École international tracks) are set at institution/programme level, not nationally standardized -- this pattern is consistent with the general European picture established elsewhere in this package but was not independently re-verified with a France-specific source this session; treat as lower confidence than the TCF findings.

application_timing.cycle: 2026-2027 academic year (entry September 2026), cited as the most recently fully-documented cycle, consistent with this package's other entries.
application_timing.major_deadline_pattern: Parcoursup: formation consultation opens mid-December (17 December 2025 cited); wish formulation opens in January (19 January 2026 cited) and closes 12 March 2026 (up to 10 vœux, up to 20 sous-vœux, no ranking required); the Fiche Avenir is finalized by lycée staff in early April; the admission phase opens 2 June 2026, with response deadlines to individual proposals running 3-5 days early in the phase, narrowing to about 2 days later -- a missed deadline forfeits the offer, though a 3-day grace window exists to request reinstatement via the platform's contact channel.
application_timing.dap_deadline_pattern: DAP, read directly from the official CERFA calendar: dossier available from 1 October 2025; deposit deadline 15 December 2025 (postmark date counts); TCF must be sat by 13 February 2026, ahead of university commissions beginning around 16 March 2026; university decisions communicated by 30 April 2026; candidate must confirm a choice by 31 May 2026.

constraints: Parcoursup: maximum 10 vœux, up to 20 sous-vœux across grouped establishments within those vœux, no required ranking/ordering of preferences.
DAP: maximum 3 university choices, set in law (Article D.612-16, Code de l'éducation) -- a materially lower ceiling than Parcoursup's 10 for the same admissions cycle.

No cap was found on Sciences Po's or École Polytechnique's separate direct-application portals (single-institution applications, not multi-choice platforms, so not directly comparable to Parcoursup/DAP choice limits).
No evidence was found of an overall cap spanning Parcoursup, DAP, and a direct-institution application together for the same applicant in one cycle.
application_strategy_constraints.explanation: A foreign-diploma DAP-track applicant has structurally fewer 'shots' (3) than a French-Bac/Parcoursup-track applicant (10) applying in the same cycle -- a real, concrete, and non-obvious asymmetry, since the two caps sit in different legal instruments and were not designed relative to each other.

personal_statement_essays.role: Parcoursup: the 'projet de formation motivé' is a per-vœu free-text field, capped at 1,500 characters, no attachments or formatting, required 'when the formation requests it' -- described in sources reviewed as very frequent for BTS, BUT, CPGE, IFSI, and by extension most sélective and 'en tension' vœux, but not confirmed as strictly universal across every non-selective Licence vœu. DAP dossier: no essay or motivation-letter field was identified in the official CERFA form read this session.
personal_statement_essays.explanation: This is a real, if short, motivation-narrative mechanism attached to the Parcoursup vœu system itself -- a materially different (more broadly present, though much shorter) pattern than the Netherlands, where a motivation letter is essentially confined to numerus fixus programmes only. The DAP-track dossier, by contrast, is essentially non-narrative (diploma, transcripts, access attestation, TCF result) -- a thinner evidentiary picture than the Parcoursup track's livret-plus-Fiche-Avenir-plus-projet-motivé combination. Whether Sciences Po's separate international-track application includes an essay component was not confirmed in the specific page fetched this session.

recommendation_letters.role: Not a Parcoursup platform mechanism -- multiple sources confirm no field exists on the platform itself to submit one, structurally similar to the 'not a baseline requirement' pattern already established for the Netherlands, Germany, and Italy, and a real difference from the US. Not listed among the DAP dossier's required documents in the official CERFA form.
recommendation_letters.explanation: Individual selective formations or schools may value or separately request a recommendation outside the Parcoursup mechanism entirely, but this was not confirmed as common or rare with precision this session. Not confirmed either way for Sciences Po's or École Polytechnique's separate direct-application tracks this session -- treat as unresolved rather than assumed absent for those specific elite tracks.

extracurricular_activities.role: Not an independently-weighted admissions factor for ordinary Licence entry. The Fiche Avenir's brief 'engagements et responsabilités' field is the closest structural analogue to a US-style activities signal for French-Bac-track applicants.
extracurricular_activities.nuance: This field is teacher-authored (part of the professeur principal's common appraisal), not a student-authored activities list -- a genuinely different mechanism and authorship model than the US Common App Activities List, extending RULE-ADMISSIONS-008's pattern (extracurricular weight is admissions-system dependent) with another non-US/UK data point. For DAP-track applicants, no mechanism for extracurricular evidence was identified in the CERFA dossier at all -- activities appear to play no structural role whatsoever in that track. For sélective Parcoursup vœux, activity evidence can surface indirectly within the projet de formation motivé, similar in spirit to the Netherlands' motivation-letter pattern for numerus fixus programmes.

interviews_tests_portfolios.pattern: PASS/LAS second-year progression includes a confirmed, mandatory oral-exam round (the 'second groupe d'épreuves') for candidates in the mid-ranking band -- a subject-knowledge oral exam, not a general admissions interview. CPGE entry itself is dossier-only in the sources found, with no separate interview at the entry stage, though some individual schools reportedly offer an interview as an alternative signal specifically for foreign-schooled applicants whose bulletins are hard to interpret. Sciences Po's international Bachelor track and art/design/conservatoire-style programmes plausibly involve interviews and/or portfolio submission respectively, by strong structural analogy to the pattern already confirmed for the Netherlands, Germany, and Italy.
interviews_tests_portfolios.when_applicable: PASS/LAS second-year progression only (confirmed); CPGE entry generally not (confirmed dossier-only), with a possible school-specific exception for foreign-schooled applicants (secondary-corroborated only); Sciences Po international track and art/design/conservatoire programmes not independently re-verified with a France-specific source this session -- treat as lower confidence than the PASS/LAS finding.

restricted_selective_programmes.explanation: At least three independently-varying restriction mechanisms coexist in France and must not be conflated. (1) PASS/LAS 'numerus apertus' for Medicine, Pharmacy, Dentistry, Midwifery, and Physiotherapy (MMOPK): the old fixed national numerus clausus was replaced in 2020 by a flexible, per-university capacity figure set jointly with the Regional Health Agency (ARS), reflecting local training/internship capacity rather than a national quota. First-year PASS or LAS entry is via ordinary Parcoursup registration; the actual restriction bites at second-year progression, a separate, internal, competitive process per university -- two 'groupes d'épreuves' (continuous assessment plus written exams, then oral exams for the mid-ranking band), with final admission determined by rank order, not raw average. A further reform reportedly planned for 2027 would replace the PASS/LAS structure with a new single pathway; exact mechanics were not detailed in sources reviewed this session. (2) CPGE-to-Grande-École 'concours': CPGE entry itself (via Parcoursup, dossier-based) is not capacity-limited the way PASS/LAS is; the real competitive bottleneck is a separate concours two years later, run entirely outside Parcoursup by inter-school exam consortia, for entry to a specific Grande École. (3) 'Licences en tension': nominally non-selective Licences (Droit, STAPS, Psychologie, and Éco-gestion commonly cited) that a université may, under the 2018 loi ORE, rank by attendus-fit when demand exceeds capacity, without the Licence ever being formally reclassified 'sélective'.
example_fields: Médecine, Maïeutique (midwifery), Odontologie, Pharmacie -- PASS/LAS numerus apertus, second-year progression restricted
Droit, STAPS, Psychologie, Économie-Gestion -- commonly-cited 'licences en tension' examples, ranked by attendus-fit only when oversubscribed
CPGE-track Grandes Écoles (engineering, business, ENS, military, veterinary schools, École des Chartes, etc.) -- concours-restricted two years after CPGE entry, outside Parcoursup
Many post-bac Grande École/business/engineering-school Parcoursup vœux -- 'formations sélectives' with their own frais de dossier and school-specific tests/interviews feeding the Parcoursup decision

admissions_decision_model.dominant_model: Genuinely three-way, arguably richer than the two-way bifurcation found in the Netherlands, and this split is the single most important structural fact about the French system for ORYN to encode correctly alongside the platform-choice split in A_admissions_architecture.
admissions_decision_model.explanation: (1) Ordinary, non-oversubscribed Licences: closer to a threshold/right-based model -- Bac (or a DAP-recognized equivalent) plus available capacity equals admission, no competitive ranking. (2) 'Licences en tension': threshold-eligible pool then ranked against the mention's attendus by the université's own commission once demand exceeds capacity -- a soft, administrative selection layer bolted onto a nominally open-access category. (3) Formally 'sélective' formations (CPGE, BTS, BUT, most Grande-École/business/engineering vœux, IFSI, and PASS/LAS to an extent): explicitly competitive ranking via each formation's own confidential selection process, submitted through Parcoursup as the routing layer only. Layered independently on top: DAP-track admission runs an entirely separate process -- each of up to 3 chosen universities' own commission evaluates the dossier against its 'capacités d'accueil,' outside the sélective/non-sélective Parcoursup taxonomy altogether, since DAP-track applicants are not on Parcoursup for this purpose. No disclosed numeric weighting formula exists at the national level for any of these tracks.

safe_inferences: It is safe to infer that the applicable platform for a France-bound applicant is determined by diploma track (French/European Bac vs. foreign diploma) and, for foreign-diploma holders, country of residence -- not by a single universal 'the French application system.'
It is safe to infer that Parcoursup registration alone never constitutes an admission decision for sélective formations, mirroring Studielink's role in the Netherlands.

It is safe to infer that a Turkish MEB-only applicant resident in Türkiye is very likely on the DAP/Études en France track, not Parcoursup, for ordinary Licence entry, capped at 3 university choices rather than 10.

It is safe to infer that the DAP dossier's documentary requirements (diploma, transcripts, conditional access attestation, TCF) are thinner and more purely academic than the Parcoursup track's livret-plus-Fiche-Avenir-plus-motivation combination -- no essay, no teacher appraisal, no activities signal identified for DAP.

It is safe to infer that PASS/LAS first-year entry (via Parcoursup) and second-year progression (via a separate internal ranked-exam process) are two different admissions events with two different selection logics, not one continuous process.
It is safe to infer that CPGE entry and Grande École 'concours' entry are two different, temporally separated events with different mechanisms and must be described separately.
unsafe_inferences: Do not assume Parcoursup is 'the' French application platform for any student headed to French higher education -- materially wrong for most foreign-diploma applicants.
Do not assume ENIC-NARIC France's comparability attestation is a required input to first-year DAP-track Licence admission; it was not listed as required in the official CERFA form reviewed.

Do not assume a Turkish MEB Lise Diploması's DAP 'Situation A' vs. 'Situation B' classification without checking the YKS-access-attestation question directly -- this research reasoned toward Situation B by analogy to R2.1's YKS findings but did not confirm it with a Turkey-specific source.

Do not treat Parcoursup's 'oui, si' response as a rejection or as equivalent to the UK/Netherlands' grade-conditional offer -- it specifically conditions admission on accepting a remediation pathway, not on a grade target.

Do not assume attendus function as a hard prerequisite gate the way Dutch vakkeneisen or UK 'essential' subjects can -- official guidance explicitly frames them as non-exclusionary, though individual sélective formations may bind their own local requirements more tightly.
Do not assume PASS/LAS's numerus apertus is a fixed national figure like the old numerus clausus -- it is set per-university with the regional health authority and can vary substantially.
Do not conflate CPGE-entry selectivity with the later, separate, and far more consequential Grande École concours.
Do not assume the DAP 3-choice cap applies to Parcoursup, or vice versa.

Do not assume recommendation letters and personal narrative are absent from every French pathway -- Parcoursup's projet de formation motivé is a real, if short, motivation mechanism many formations do require, a meaningfully different picture from the Netherlands' near-total absence of narrative motivation outside numerus fixus.

eligibility_competitiveness_fit.eligibility: Splits by track: for French/European Bac holders it is largely a qualification check (holding, or being on track to hold, the Bac) plus, for sélective formations, meeting that formation's published attendus profile; for DAP-track applicants it is governed by the Situation A/B/C framework plus the target université's own commission judgment against stated capacity.
eligibility_competitiveness_fit.competitiveness: Varies sharply by category in a way that requires at least three states, not two: largely absent for ordinary non-oversubscribed Licences (closer to a right, once eligible); present but administratively soft for 'licences en tension' (ranked by attendus-fit only when oversubscribed); and fully present, dossier-and-often-test-driven, for formally sélective formations and for PASS/LAS second-year progression specifically.
eligibility_competitiveness_fit.fit: Expressed primarily through spécialité-to-mention alignment (does the retained coursework match the target field) for French-Bac-track applicants, and -- for sélective formations only -- through the short projet de formation motivé. No equivalent fit signal exists in the DAP dossier beyond the diploma/transcript record itself.

counselor_actions: Determine the applicable platform first: is the student preparing a French or European Baccalauréat (Parcoursup), or a foreign diploma (DAP via Études en France/Campus France if resident in one of the ~72 listed countries -- confirmed to include Türkiye -- or paper DAP via embassy otherwise)?

For a Turkish MEB-only student: register via turquie.campusfrance.org, plan around the materially lower 3-university DAP cap (vs. Parcoursup's 10), and confirm the TCF French-language test requirement and timeline (sat by mid-February for an April-decision cycle) unless an independent DELF/DALF B2+ exemption applies.
Do not assume ENIC-NARIC France pre-clears a Turkish diploma before DAP submission -- check directly with the target université's admissions office instead.

For French-Bac-track students targeting sélective or 'en tension' formations, help prepare a substantive, field-specific projet de formation motivé (1,500-character limit) and confirm which two spécialités best align with the target mention's attendus.

Determine early whether any target formation is PASS/LAS (plan for a first-year Parcoursup entry followed by a genuinely separate, ranked, internal second-year competitive process), a 'licence en tension' (grades and attendus-fit matter more than the 'non sélective' label suggests), or CPGE (dossier-only entry now; the real competitive event is a concours two years later, run outside Parcoursup, for a different institution).

For students considering Sciences Po's or École Polytechnique's elite direct-application tracks, treat these as a third, separate architecture from both Parcoursup and DAP, with their own deadlines and fees (Sciences Po's international track: EUR 150 application fee, confirmed).

data_model_implications.notes: France requires ORYN's data model to represent, as a first-class fact, which platform even applies -- not just which threshold applies within one platform. This is a sharper requirement than any of the other six countries in this package, where a single national platform (or its confirmed absence) was the starting assumption. At minimum four scope levels are needed: (1) national/legal (loi ORE, the DAP 3-choice cap under Article D.612-16, the TCF exemption list, the ~72-country Études en France list), (2) platform (Parcoursup mechanics vs. Études en France/DAP mechanics -- genuinely different platforms with different document requirements, choice caps, and decision-makers, not variations on one system), (3) université (admissions-commission-level judgment on DAP dossiers and 'en tension' ranking thresholds), and (4) formation/programme (attendus, sélective-vs-non classification, PASS/LAS numerus apertus quotas, spécialité requirements, CPGE-vs-concours timing). A single 'France requirement' record per qualification type would be actively misleading -- the model needs 'which platform, which document set, which decision-maker' to vary by diploma type and residence before any threshold-level comparison is even meaningful.
gaps: Whether a standard MEB Lise Diploması is classified DAP 'Situation A' or 'Situation B' for Turkish applicants specifically, and what exact YKS-based evidence (if any) is expected.
Whether AP/IB/A-Level layered on a Turkish MEB record eases DAP admission the way it clearly does at Dutch universities.
Whether ENIC-NARIC France plays any role, even an optional/supportive one, in Turkish-diploma DAP admissions.
The precise current mechanics of the reported 2027 PASS/LAS reform.

Whether Sciences Po's and École Polytechnique's separate international tracks require an essay and/or recommendation letter, and whether their admitted foreign-diploma students from Études-en-France countries must separately complete Études en France afterward for visa purposes.
Exact 2027-2028 Parcoursup and DAP calendar dates (not yet published as of this research pass).

system_university_programme_override_mod.explanation: Layer 1 (national/legal): the loi ORE (2018) sets the Parcoursup/attendus/ranking framework; Article D.612-16 sets the DAP 3-choice cap; the Études en France country list and TCF exemption rules are set nationally -- no university can waive these. Layer 2 (platform): Parcoursup vs. Études en France/DAP are two structurally different platforms with different document requirements and choice limits, selected by diploma track and residence rather than by student preference -- this is the layer that has no clean analogue in the Netherlands entry, where a single platform (Studielink) applied to essentially everyone. Layer 3 (université): each institution's admissions commission sets its own DAP-dossier judgment against its own stated capacités d'accueil, and (for 'en tension' Licences) its own attendus-ranking practice -- where the same input qualification can in principle produce different outcomes at different universities, though this research did not surface a Tilburg-vs-VU-style paired example for France specifically this session. Layer 4 (formation/programme): individual formations set their own attendus emphasis, sélective-vs-non status, and (for PASS/LAS, CPGE, and most Grande-École vœux) their own selection method and capacity ceiling -- the mechanism that, as in every other country in this package, converts an otherwise threshold-based picture into a genuinely competitive one. ORYN should never present a Layer 3 or 4 fact (a specific université's DAP judgment, or a specific formation's attendus or selection method) as if it were a Layer 1 or 2 national fact.

matrix_row.main_application_architecture: Diploma-track-and-residence-determined split: Parcoursup (centralized registration/routing + fully decentralized per-formation selection) for French/European Baccalauréat holders; a separate DAP dossier -- filed via Études en France/Campus France for residents of ~72 listed countries, or on paper via embassy for others -- for foreign-diploma holders seeking ordinary Licence entry; a minority of elite institutions (Sciences Po, École Polytechnique Bachelor) run their own fully separate direct-application portals for foreign-diploma applicants
matrix_row.central_platform: Parcoursup (French/European Bac track only, registration+routing, not itself a decision-maker) and, separately, the Études en France/Campus France platform (foreign-diploma track, residents of ~72 listed countries -- carries the DAP dossier and administrative/visa-linked processing)
matrix_row.direct_applications_possible: Not as a general alternative for French/European Bac holders (Parcoursup required) or for most foreign-diploma holders in listed countries (DAP required); a small number of elite institutions (Sciences Po Bachelor's international track, École Polytechnique's Bachelor of Science) run their own direct portal specifically for foreign-diploma applicants, bypassing Parcoursup and, for the admissions decision itself, DAP
matrix_row.application_choice_limits: Parcoursup: max 10 vœux (up to 20 sous-vœux across grouped establishments), no ranking required; DAP: max 3 university choices (Article D.612-16, Code de l'éducation) -- a materially lower cap than Parcoursup for the same academic year
matrix_row.predicted_grades_role: No formal numeric predicted-grade concept nationally. Functionally closest analogue: the livret scolaire's actual in-progress première/terminale grades plus the qualitative Fiche Avenir (professeur-principal appraisal + chef d'établissement's opinion on 'capacité à réussir'), both read by admissions commissions before final Bac results are known -- real evidence, not a forward-looking prediction. DAP-track (foreign-diploma) dossiers carry no equivalent mechanism identified this session.
matrix_row.subject_prerequisites: Nationally-published 'attendus' per Licence mention (and for CPGE) describe expected competencies/subject alignment -- explicitly non-exclusionary guidance, not a hard gate, though individual formations can bind their own local specifics on top. For French-Bac students the operative real signal is which two of three spécialités were retained through terminale. No equivalent nationally-mapped foreign-curriculum-to-attendus table was found for DAP-track applicants.
matrix_row.standardized_tests: No SAT/ACT-equivalent for ordinary Licence entry. TCF (Test de Connaissance du Français) is a mandatory language-and-writing test specifically for most DAP-track (foreign-diploma) applicants. CPGE-to-Grande-École 'concours' and PASS/LAS second-year 'épreuves' are real but programme/track-specific competitive exams, not national baseline Licence requirements.
matrix_row.language_proof: Only structurally relevant for the DAP/foreign-diploma track: TCF (mandatory unless exempted -- French-official-language-country nationals/residents, substantially-French-medium prior schooling, or DELF/DALF B2+). Not required for French/European Bac holders. English-taught-programme language requirements (IELTS/TOEFL etc.) are institution/programme-set, not nationally standardized -- not independently re-verified this session.
matrix_row.essays_motivation: Parcoursup: 'projet de formation motivé,' a per-vœu 1,500-character free-text field, required when the specific formation requests it -- described as very frequent for selective formations, not confirmed as universally mandatory for every non-selective Licence vœu. DAP dossier: no essay or motivation-letter field identified in the official CERFA form.
matrix_row.recommendations: Not a Parcoursup platform mechanism (no submission field exists) and not listed among required DAP documents -- broadly absent at the structural Licence level, though individual selective institutions may request one outside these two mechanisms; not confirmed either way for elite direct-application tracks (Sciences Po, Polytechnique) this session.
matrix_row.extracurricular_role: Not an independently-weighted factor for ordinary Licence admission. The Fiche Avenir's brief 'engagements et responsabilités' field (teacher-authored, not student-authored) is the closest structural analogue for French-Bac-track applicants; no equivalent mechanism identified for DAP-track (foreign-diploma) applicants at all.
matrix_row.conditional_offers: Exists in a narrower/different sense than UK/Netherlands. Parcoursup's 'oui, si' response is a named, distinct mechanism: admission conditional on accepting a mandatory remediation/support pathway, not on final-grade attainment. Final Bac attainment itself is treated more like an implicit assumption than a formally-labeled conditional artifact (not independently confirmed with an explicit official statement this session). DAP dossiers explicitly anticipate a not-yet-obtained diploma (Situations A1/B1), with the original diploma required only at final registration -- a genuine diploma-conditional structure for that track.
matrix_row.restricted_programmes: At least three independently-varying mechanisms, not one: (1) PASS/LAS 'numerus apertus' for MMOPK health fields -- per-university capacity set with the Regional Health Agency, first-year entry via ordinary Parcoursup, second-year progression via a separate competitive ranked exam process; (2) CPGE-to-Grande-École 'concours' -- dossier-based CPGE entry via Parcoursup, but the real competitive bottleneck is a separate concours 2 years later, run entirely outside Parcoursup; (3) 'licences en tension' -- nominally non-selective Licences (Droit, STAPS, Psychologie, Éco-gestion commonly cited) that a university may rank by attendus-fit under the 2018 loi ORE when demand exceeds capacity, without being formally classified 'sélective'
matrix_row.turkiye_meb_direct_entry_complexity: High, and structurally different in kind from the other researched countries: a standard MEB Lise Diploması holder (no French/European Bac) resident in Türkiye is very likely not on the Parcoursup track at all for ordinary Licence entry -- Turkey is primary-source-confirmed (official CERFA DAP form) as one of the ~72 'Études en France' countries, meaning the applicable pathway is the DAP dossier filed via Campus France Turquie, capped at 3 university choices, gated by a mandatory TCF French-language test (Turkey is not on the French-official-language exemption list), evaluated by each university's own admissions commission with no confirmed ENIC-NARIC-France comparability step and no confirmed AP/IB/A-Level-eases-things pattern (contrast the Netherlands' clear finding on that point) -- several of these specifics are flagged gaps, not confirmed negatives
matrix_row.dominant_counselor_risk: Assuming Parcoursup is 'the' French application platform for any student headed to French higher education, when it is specifically the French/European-Baccalauréat-track platform -- a Turkish MEB-only applicant is generally routed instead through an entirely different mechanism (DAP via Études en France/Campus France, capped at 3 choices vs. Parcoursup's 10, with its own TCF language gate) that a counselor defaulting to 'just register on Parcoursup' would miss entirely

unresolved_questions: Whether a standard MEB Lise Diploması is classified DAP 'Situation A' or 'Situation B' for Turkish applicants specifically, and what exact YKS-based evidence (if any) is expected -- reasoned toward Situation B by analogy to R2.1's findings, not confirmed by a Turkey-naming source.
Whether AP/IB/A-Level layered on a Turkish MEB record eases DAP admission the way it clearly does at Dutch universities.

Whether ENIC-NARIC France plays any role, even an optional/supportive one, in Turkish-diploma DAP admissions (its own site was unreachable this session -- a certificate error, not a confirmed absence).
Whether AEFE-network or IB schools in Türkiye follow an identical spécialité list/curriculum to metropolitan France (carried forward from R2.1, unresolved there too).
The precise current mechanics of the reported 2027 PASS/LAS reform.

Whether Sciences Po's and École Polytechnique's separate international tracks require an essay and/or recommendation letter, and whether their admitted foreign-diploma students from Études-en-France countries must separately complete Études en France afterward for visa purposes.
Exact 2027-2028 Parcoursup and DAP calendar dates (not yet published as of this research pass).
Whether the 'projet de formation motivé' field is in practice mandatory for literally every Parcoursup vœu or only for those the formation flags as requiring it.
Precise, current English-taught-programme language-proficiency thresholds at a representative sample of French institutions.

Whether a numeric cap exists spanning Parcoursup, DAP, and direct-institution applications combined for a single applicant in one cycle (no evidence of one was found, but this was not exhaustively tested against an official source).

A_admissions_architecture.primary_application_route: Two entirely separate application systems, gated by LOCAL vs. NON-LOCAL status (not by qualification type). (1) JUPAS (Joint University Programmes Admissions System, jupas.edu.hk) is the shared national platform used by 9 JUPAS-participating institutions, but it is open only to local applicants holding (past and/or current) HKDSE Examination results who are not already enrolled full-time in a JUPAS bachelor's programme. (2) Non-JUPAS is not a single shared platform at all — it is a label for each institution's own separate direct-application scheme, run through that university's own online application portal (e.g. HKU's own International/Non-JUPAS system, CUHK's own Non-JUPAS/International system at admission.cuhk.edu.hk, HKUST's own system at join.hkust.edu.hk). As of the 2020 JUPAS cycle, in accordance with HKSAR Government policy, ALL non-local applicants — regardless of whether they hold HKDSE results — must apply via non-JUPAS at each university individually, not via JUPAS. Non-JUPAS also covers local applicants whose eligibility rests on combining HKDSE with another qualification, or who hold no HKDSE result at all.
A_admissions_architecture.centralized_or_decentralized: Bifurcated by applicant type, more sharply than any of the six countries in the existing package. For the LOCAL/HKDSE segment: centralized application (JUPAS platform, shared fee schedule, shared timeline) feeding a centralized-ish matching algorithm, but with admission ratings still set independently per programme. For the NON-LOCAL/international segment (which is where essentially every Turkish MEB/IB/A-Level applicant sits): fully decentralized — no shared platform, no shared timeline, no shared fee, no shared application form across the 9 institutions. A student applying to HKU, CUHK and HKUST as an international applicant is filing three unrelated applications.
major_application_platforms: JUPAS (jupas.edu.hk) — shared platform for local/HKDSE applicants across 9 participating institutions; NOT used by non-local applicants under any circumstance since the 2020 cycle

Each university's own non-JUPAS/International Admissions portal (HKU, CUHK, HKUST, PolyU, CityU, EdUHK, HKBU, LingnanU, and others each run their own) — the required route for essentially all non-local/international applicants, including Turkish MEB/IB/A-Level holders
A_admissions_architecture.direct_university_application_possible: For non-local/international applicants this is not merely possible, it is the ONLY route — there is no centralized alternative available to them at all. For local applicants the reverse is true in the ordinary case: JUPAS is required for anyone relying on HKDSE results alone, and direct/non-JUPAS application is reserved for local applicants combining HKDSE with another qualification or holding no HKDSE result.
A_admissions_architecture.application_limit_if_any: Within JUPAS: up to 20 programme choices, organized into 5 preference bands (Band A = choices 1-3, Band B = choices 4-6, and so on) — see application_strategy_constraints. Within non-JUPAS: no shared cross-university limit exists because there is no shared platform; each university sets its own internal choice count on its own application (this was not independently confirmed at a specific number for HKU/CUHK/HKUST in sources reviewed this pass and should not be assumed uniform).
